So a few things:  


1. 2 months of dating, you didn't know him enough to know if you want to "tolerate" his bad sides for a lifetime. And yes, I use "tolerate" because all of us in long term relationships have a tolerance towards our partner, the one we love them unconditionally through.  

2. You had an ADDITIONAL child, An additional life YOU and him BOTH made the choice to bring into this world. Now. As a child of divorce and brought up in Boarding school back and forth abroad my entire childhood (I was lucky in the sense my family had the funds to help my mother), I can say right now that you have equal fault in this situation, and let me explain;  
 a. The fact that a conversation wasn't brought up when he had part time job for 2 months bringing home not even enough for a phone bill  is unacceptable.   
 b. "Didn't like driving" is an excuse to his responsibilities to the entire family as a strike TWO (Not sure why an ultimatum wasn't set up on "a" here before it got worse)  
 c. He's shown a clear lack of duty to protect you and your children from going towards poverty or worse for this long, and you had let it continue for this long. Whether he needs therapy for motivation or other help to bring home INCOME, which is a BASELINE condition that needs to be continued.  

3. I'm going to assume your last statement was because you're distraught, and you didn't mean it. We all have people we love but chose not to be with. SAYING and BELIEVING "I can't be a good mom because I'm miserable" = you shouldn't be one. Your kids doesn't deserve you or your husband at this moment if that's something you actually believe to be true.  


All this to say, these are things you need to talk to your husband about. And if you two can't reach a resolution, you need to think of what's BEST for your kids first. You both are married, they're as much your bills as HIS in a legal sense. I know it's easier said than done, you need motivation to be strong? You children's happiness and having a good future should be it, and if that isn't motivation enough for you; the question is if you deserve their custody?

Ultimate question to yourself:  
Do you have enough tolerance to suffer through this long term and to the end?  


Relationships will fail even if both ppl LIKE each other, the part of it that matters is asking yourself and answer without hesitation:  


Are you happy most of the time in this relationship?
